name: Colorado River (Diamond Creek to Pearce Ferry)
gaugeName: Colorado River above Diamond Creek near Peach Springs, AZ
blurb: Lower Gorge of the Grand Canyon from Diamond Creek (Hualapai land) to Pearce Ferry in Lake Mead NRA. NPS Diamond Creek permit required.

sections.notes: NPS: 'It includes 52 river miles of smooth and white water'; noncommercial trips from Diamond Creek (river mile 225) 'take 2 to 5 days'. NPS Diamond Creek permit required; Hualapai Tribe fees to launch at Diamond Creek. This listed trip ends at Pearce Ferry, a river-trip take-out only; launching there is prohibited. NPS also lists South Cove as an alternative endpoint, but it is not the endpoint or mileage of this section.
sections.routeReview: Diamond Creek is an approximate, permit-required access area on Hualapai land. This access map does not show an exact landing connection, road route, or reviewed river course.

notices.title: Diamond Creek: arrange permits in advance
notices.text: Diamond Creek is on Hualapai land. Arrange tribal permits and fees for people, boats and vehicles before the trip, as well as the required NPS river permit. Check Diamond Creek Road conditions with the Tribe; the unpaved road is vulnerable to washouts. The map marker locates the access area, not an exact shoreline ramp.
notices.sourceName: National Park Service — Diamond Creek trip and permit guidance

putInAccess.sourceName: Hualapai Tribe — Diamond Creek brochure; NPS river-permit guidance
putInAccess.note: The Tribe’s own brochure identifies Diamond Creek take-out, the access road, and permit requirements. NPS explicitly documents launches and take-outs and provides a digitized Boat Launch point with unknown accuracy. Reviewed imagery places that point in the gravel landing/staging area beside the river; it is not a surveyed shoreline pin. Keep Hualapai authority and advance permits explicit. No road, landing connector, channel route or navigation approval is inferred.
putInAccess.directions: Arrange Hualapai access permits and tribal fees before your trip, in addition to the required NPS river permit. From Peach Springs, use Diamond Creek Road (Indian Route 6), roughly 19 miles unpaved. Ask the Tribe about road and flood conditions before driving. The marker shows the landing area, not a fixed water-edge ramp.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: NPS Public POIs, OBJECTID 10448 'Pearce Ferry Boat Launch' (Boat Launch)
takeOutAccess.note: NPS Public POIs, OBJECTID 10448 'Pearce Ferry Boat Launch' (Boat Launch) is the managing agency's own point. Legal boating access: NPS Lake Mead NRA: South Cove Launch Ramp page (section 'Pearce Ferry Takeout', last updated Aug 20, 2026) (https://www.nps.gov/places/south-cove-launch-ramp.htm): 'The boat ramp at Pearce Ferry is for Grand Canyon river trip takeouts only. Launching watercraft is not allowed at Pearce Ferry.' NPS Grand Canyon: 'River runners can take-out at either South Cove or Pearce Ferry.' Imagery: Esri World Imagery z19 checked 2026-10-25 (research/raw/imagery/pearce_ferry_boat_launch.png): Point is on the paved ramp lane that runs down to the river; boats are pulled up at the bottom of the ramp. NHD flowline 98 m away. Take-out only: NPS prohibits launching watercraft at Pearce Ferry.
takeOutAccess.bankSourceName: USGS NHD High Resolution flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
takeOutAccess.bankNote: Facing downstream (flow bearing ~329), the point is left of the NHD centreline (98 m).
